title: Alkanes: Conformations, Radical Halogenation, & Selectivity
topics: Ethane Conformations: Staggered (θ = 60°, D_3d) vs Eclipsed (θ = 0°, Torsional Strain = 12.5 kJ/mol)
Free Radical Halogenation Mechanism (Initiation, Propagation, Termination)
Halogen Reactivity vs Selectivity (F₂ > Cl₂ > Br₂ > I₂; Br₂ Selectivity: 3°:2°:1° = 1600:82:1)
quickSummary: Staggered ethane is 12.5 kJ/mol more stable than eclipsed due to minimal torsional strain. Halogenation proceeds via free radical chain mechanism. Bromination is highly selective (3°:2°:1° = 1600:82:1); Chlorination is unselective (5:3.8:1).
summary: Master ethane conformational dynamics, free radical halogenation mechanism, and halogen selectivity ratios.

conceptBreakdown.title: 1.1 Conformations of Ethane (Newman & Sawhorse)

summaryBox.title: Ethane Conformations
summaryBox.takeaway: Staggered (θ = 60°) is 12.5 kJ/mol (3.0 kcal/mol) more stable than Eclipsed (θ = 0°) due to minimal torsional strain.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
ETHANE CONFORMATIONAL SPECTRUM (C₂H₆)
                                       │
         ┌─────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────┐
         ▼                                                           ▼
   STAGGERED CONFORMATION                                      ECLIPSED CONFORMATION
   ├── Dihedral Angle (θ) = 60°                                ├── Dihedral Angle (θ) = 0°
   ├── Maximum spatial separation of C-H bonds                 ├── Overlapping C-H bonds
   ├── Minimal Torsional Strain                                ├── Max Torsional Strain (12.5 kJ/mol)
   └── MORE STABLE by 12.5 kJ/mol                              └── LESS STABLE (Energy Barrier)
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Staggered Conformation ($\theta = 60^\circ$)**: Maximum spatial separation of $\text{C-H}$ bonds, minimal torsional strain, and possesses $D_{3d}$ symmetry. It is $\mathbf{12.5\text{ kJ/mol}}$ more stable than the eclipsed conformer.
• **Eclipsed Conformation ($\theta = 0^\circ$)**: Maximum electrostatic repulsion between overlapping $\text{C-H}$ electron pairs (**Torsional Strain**).
• **Rotational Barrier**: The $12.5\text{ kJ/mol}$ barrier is small enough to permit rapid rotation ($10^{11}\text{ rotations/sec}$) at room temperature.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 1.2 Free Radical Halogenation & Selectivity Ratios
conceptBreakdown.title: 1.2 Free Radical Halogenation & Selectivity Ratios
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
HALOGEN SELECTIVITY RATIOS (3° : 2° : 1°)

• Chlorination (25°C): 3° : 2° : 1° = 5.0 : 3.8 : 1.0 (Low Selectivity)
• Bromination (127°C): 3° : 2° : 1° = 1600 : 82 : 1.0 (High Selectivity)

Monochlorination Product Yield = (Number of n°-H) × (Relative Reactivity of n°-H)
conceptBreakdown.content:
1. **Mechanism**: Initiation ($h\nu \to 2\text{X}^\bullet$), Propagation ($\text{X}^\bullet + \text{R-H} \to \text{R}^\bullet + \text{HX}$, rate-determining for $\text{Br}_2$), and Termination (radical recombination).
2. **Hammond Postulate**: Bromination is endothermic and has a late, product-like transition state, making it highly selective for $3^\circ$ hydrogens ($1600:1$). Chlorination is exothermic with an early transition state, leading to low selectivity ($5:1$).
3. **Reactivity Order**: $\text{F}_2 > \text{Cl}_2 > \text{Br}_2 > \text{I}_2$ (Fluorination explosive; Iodination reversible, requiring $\text{HNO}_3/\text{HIO}_3$ oxidants).

quickRevision: Staggered ethane is 12.5 kJ/mol more stable than eclipsed.
Iodination requires HNO₃/HIO₃ to remove HI and drive equilibrium forward.
